items.what: Invalid date values in If-Unmodified-Since and If-Range must be ignored, returning a normal 200 full-body response (no 412, no 206); the instruction never mentions malformed date handling.
items.quote: lastmod = 'not a valid HTTP-date' ... assert 200 == resp.status

items.what: If-Unmodified-Since unsatisfied must yield status 412 both with and without a Range header; the instruction only says 'honored', never naming 412 or that the check applies also when no Range is present.

If-Range semantics: when the If-Range date does not match the file mtime the server must return the full file with 200 (even with a Range header); when it matches (future date vs old mtime) it must return 206 with Content-Range.
items.quote: assert 200 == resp.status ... assert 206 == resp.status; assert resp.headers['Content-Range'] == 'bytes 2-12/13'

items.what: An over-large tail range (bytes=-99999999999999) must be clamped to the whole file but still answered with 206 and Content-Range 'bytes 0-<size-1>/<size>'; the instruction says 'returning the whole file', which could reasonably mean 200.

Exact Content-Range header casing/format 'Content-Range: bytes <start>-<end>/<size>' asserted on 206 responses; format is given in the issue, casing 'Content-Range' is the conventional spelling (tests use resp.headers which is case-insensitive, so guessable).

reason: The core Range fixes (Content-Range, 416, tail clamping) and basic conditional-header honoring follow directly from the issue, but the tests additionally pin down invalid-date handling (must be ignored, returning 200), the 412 status for failed If-Unmodified-Since, and exact If-Range match/mismatch semantics (200 full body vs 206 partial), none of which the instruction states.
